summary.text: Steven Horsford is the Democratic incumbent in Nevada's 4th District, serving since 2019 and previously from 2013 to 2015. A Las Vegas native, he served in the Nevada Senate, including as majority leader, and led the Culinary Training Academy of Las Vegas before entering Congress. He sits on the Ways and Means Committee and chaired the Congressional Black Caucus from 2023 to 2025.

paragraphs.text: Horsford was born and raised in Las Vegas; his official biography says his mother immigrated to the United States and that he lost his father when he was 19. He graduated from Clark High School and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Nevada, Reno.

According to Wikipedia, he began working at the Las Vegas marketing and consulting firm R&R Partners in 1996. He was later executive director of the Culinary Training Academy of Las Vegas, which his official biography describes as the largest job training program in Nevada.

Horsford served in the Nevada State Senate from 2004 to 2012, including as Majority Leader from 2009 to 2012; his official biography describes him as the first African American Majority Leader of the Nevada State Senate.
He won Nevada's 4th District in 2012, defeating Danny Tarkanian 50.1% to 42.1%, and served one term before losing re-election in 2014 to Cresent Hardy, 48.5% to 45.8%.

After leaving Congress, Horsford started a small business, and his official biography cites a workforce development program for young people in North Las Vegas with Intel and a food recovery program with Three Square. Wikipedia reports that he rejoined R&R Partners.

Horsford was elected again to the open 4th District seat in 2018. In 2025-2026 he serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Health and Social Security subcommittees), and he earlier served on committees including Financial Services, Armed Services, Budget and Natural Resources.
He chaired the Congressional Black Caucus from January 2023 to January 2025. His official biography says he has three children.
